text:
I almost drowned my own interface.

Every order you could possibly place sitting on screen at once. Echo, troponin, ANA, TSH, twelve lead, physical exam by region, all of it stacked on top of a man lying in a bed who just wants someone to figure out what’s wrong with him.

It looked thorough. It felt like chaos.

Nobody learns anything staring at forty labels at once. You don’t memorize a wall. You get lost in it, and your brain shuts the whole thing out to protect itself.

So now you can collapse it. Hide a category once you’ve cleared it. Let the ones that matter right now stay in front of you, and let the rest wait their turn.

The point was never to show you everything medicine has. The point is to show you what this patient needs, in the order a real clinician would ask for it.

That’s the difference between a wall of information and a room you can actually think in.
